plotSections.title: Gerk and the Mother's Prayer
bullets: Sylan reveals that a journal he found contained a passage about the Navi searching for a child whose mother died but who survived.
Sylan explains that a meditation in Jotunheim revealed Gerk as the child described in the journal and suggested that Gerk was a keeper who would open the doors.
Dana recalls the prophecy heard repeatedly in the stronghold, describing a gate opening, eight being torn asunder, keys lying dormant, arches as doors, and a mysterious burden.
The prophecy is identified as the Mother's Prayer or Mother's Prophecy and is connected to Gerk as the possible child and keeper.

Plymouth and Kit Anger become significantly more interested in Gerk after hearing Sylan's explanation. Plymouth approaches and examines Gerk while asking whether he is the one described by the Mother's Prayer.
Gerk cannot confirm that the prophecy refers to him, while Plymouth suggests that events may already be in motion beyond Gerk's awareness.

plotSections.title: Sylan's Journal
bullets: Sylan clarifies that the source was a relatively recent handwritten journal rather than one of Nevarr's books or tomes.
The journal appears to have been written by multiple hands over time.
It described the Navi searching for a surviving child whose mother had died and also contained a plot against Sylan's family that later occurred.
Sylan does not recall any explicit prophecy in the journal itself and still possesses it.

chronologicalEvents: Sylan and Gerk discuss whether the group should be told that Sylan believes Gerk is special and chosen; Gerk decides to reveal it.
Sylan explains that a journal he found described the Navi searching for a child whose mother had died while the child survived.
Sylan explains that a meditation in Jotunheim revealed Gerk as the child and suggested that he was a keeper who would open the doors.
The DM establishes that the journal was handwritten by multiple authors and was relatively recent.
Sylan says the journal also contained a successful plot against his family but no explicit prophecy that he can recall.
Dana recalls the Mother's Prayer heard echoing through the stronghold, including references to gates, eight being torn asunder, keys, arches, and doors.
The Mother's Prayer is identified as the Mother's Prayer or Mother's Prophecy and connected to the child and keeper described by Sylan.
Plymouth approaches Gerk and examines him while asking whether he is the individual described by the Mother's Prayer.
Gerk says he cannot know whether the prophecy refers to him, while Plymouth warns that events may already be unfolding beyond Gerk's awareness.

notes: Sylan believes Gerk is the surviving child described in the journal about whom the Navi were searching.
Sylan's meditation in Jotunheim identified Gerk as the child and suggested that he is a keeper who will open the doors between realms.
The Mother's Prayer or Mother's Prophecy appears to concern Gerk, though Gerk does not know whether he is the individual described by it.
Plymouth questioned and examined Gerk in an attempt to determine whether he is the person described in the prophecy.

The prophecy is now believed to be connected to Gerk as the child and possible keeper who will open the doors.
